frame.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / game UI asset. Create an ORIGINAL production-ready tutorial popup BACKPLATE for the small isometric puzzle game shown in reference image 2. This is the UI skin that will be used for all three tutorial pages. Reference image 1 is an EDIT TARGET for composition only: completely restyle its interface. Reference image 2 is the actual game and is the style authority.
Canvas: very wide 2:1 landscape, ideally 1920x960, front-facing orthographic UI, straight edges, no perspective distortion of the overall panel.
Visual style: charming clean low-poly toy-block puzzle game, chunky beveled off-white and light-gray platforms with charcoal-black extruded side faces, a few saturated yellow-gold arrow/tile accents and one small bright blue cube motif. Warm ivory main surface, clean subtle ambient shadows, matte surfaces, simple geometric construction. Make it look like an interface constructed from the game's real tiles. The final image should feel playful, minimal, polished, readable, not an enterprise dashboard.
Layout MUST match reference 1 proportions: one large blank title strip across top 0%-17% height; a large flat empty SCREEN WINDOW in the LEFT body, rectangle approximately x=3% to60%, y=20% to91%; THREE separate blank instruction slab surfaces stacked in the RIGHT body, x=63% to98%, y=20%-40%,44%-64%,68%-88%; a shallow blank footer strip at bottom92%-99%. The screenshot window interior must be plain uniform charcoal, with thin ivory beveled rim, so a real screenshot can be composited over it later. Right instruction slabs should have very subtle pale-gray face variation, thick simple chamfered corners and small dark lower edges, with LOTS of empty flat readable writing area. Decorative blue cube and a short path of white arrow tiles may sit in the upper-right corner of the title strip without intruding into title space. Keep the useful surfaces front-facing and unskewed.
REMOVE ALL writing, letters, Japanese, numbers, old screenshot markings, colored badges, and typography from reference 1. Output NO text at all. Do NOT include a button: it will be a separate sprite. Do NOT add any new gameplay screenshot or imaginary scene inside the screen window. No textures, no weathering, no stone ruins, no wood, no parchment, no mint-green branding, no navy dashboard, no neon circuitry, no ornate science fiction. Keep everything cropped neatly inside the 2:1 rectangular canvas. Opaque backplate, no transparent outer area. The requested output is the complete reusable illustrated skin, not a mockup floating in a room.

button.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE standalone wide horizontal button background SPRITE for the isometric low-poly puzzle game in the reference screenshot. Transparent background is REQUIRED. Ideally 1024x256 (4:1) or similarly very wide landscape. The button itself nearly fills the full canvas, leaving only a minimal transparent margin for the shadow. Front-facing, not angled isometric overall. Its face is a clean vivid golden yellow slab, with chamfered geometric corners, soft bright bevel on top/left, charcoal-black thick extruded bottom edge and muted gray right side like the game's block platforms. Matte simple toy-block rendering, restrained shadows, excellent contrast for dark Japanese text that will be overlaid later. No text, no letters, no symbols, no icon, no arrows, no labels, no decorative props, no frame around the canvas, no duplicate buttons. This will be the shared close/resume button. Keep the middle 75% of the face perfectly plain and flat for a label; make left and right cap geometry visually consistent so it can be sliced horizontally. Match the white/gray/charcoal/yellow/blue clean low-poly game aesthetic rather than glossy app UI.

composition: Unity Canvas composites the original captured gameplay pixels and Japanese labels over the generated frame. The same generated skin is shared by first_stage, boss_stage, jump and the common resume button.
runtime: StageStartPopup.prefab and PopupCloseButton.prefab consume the generated theme.
